scope: Real Windows 40000-path Git filename streaming and sandbox staging workload
assertions: All four filename lanes retain 40000 actual file entries and 34988890 NUL-delimited bytes, above 32 MiB.
Standalone and scheduled snapshots use streaming manifests; metadata remains below 4096 bytes.
All 40000 staged payloads and legal Windows special names are byte-checked; late-added file is excluded.
A real shallow Git baseline and second staging delete all 40000 paths; generated shell commands stay below 16 KiB and scheduler active/queued/inflight/cache counts drain to zero.
Fixture honors provider timeoutMs: Windows total 30 minutes, per-transfer command 10 minutes; POSIX test/transfer budgets remain unchanged.

history.cause: The local fixture ignored post-upload timeoutMs and imposed a hidden 120-second shell deadline. The real xargs child finished naturally before test cleanup; the failed parent result was retained.

limits: Actual Git Bash/GNU tar on NTFS, with local simulated provider transport; not a live cloud provider or production deployment.
Long-path Git and autocrlf settings are scoped to disposable fixtures; no global Git configuration was changed.
Windows-inexpressible newline/wildcard/trailing-space filenames retain their POSIX branch but were not executed on this host.
Ancestor guards do not claim descriptor-atomic containment against concurrent namespace changes.
Earlier timeout and Unicode/exclusion failures remain historical diagnostics; this pass does not erase them.
Raw ignored logs/JSON may not be present in another checkout.
